question: Test at most 8 of the combinations of exposure 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 s and laser power 20, 40, 60 %. Among the conditions satisfying SNR >= 20 (T050 definition), no saturated pixel, and at least 90% of the T077_ref.csv reference peaks detected, select the one with the lowest dose, where dose = power x exposure x 0.01 mJ.
criteria: PROC(<=8 calls) + EXACT(chosen combination) / post-hoc GT
answer_text:
To find the optimal measurement conditions, I tested 8 combinations of laser power (20%, 40%, 60%) and exposure time (0.25 s, 0.5 s, 1.0 s, 2.0 s). The criteria for selection were an SNR $\ge 20$, no saturated pixels, and detection of at least 90% (i.e., all 9) of the reference peaks from `T077_ref.csv`.

The results are summarized below:

| Power (%) | Exposure (s) | Dose (mJ) | SNR | Saturated | Peaks Detected / Total | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20 | 0.25 | 0.05 | 50.50 | No | 4/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 20 | 0.5 | 0.10 | 101.29 | No | 5/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 40 | 0.25 | 0.10 | 91.10 | No | 7/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 60 | 0.25 | 0.15 | 147.32 | No | 5/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 60 | 0.5 | 0.30 | 160.20 | No | 5/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 40 | 1.0 | 0.40 | 191.36 | No | 6/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| 20 | 2.0 | 0.40 | 179.74 | No | 5/9 | Fail (Peaks) |
| **60** | **1.0** | **0.60** | **197.61** | **No** | **9/9** | **Pass** |

Among the tested combinations, only the condition with a laser power of 60% and an exposure time of 1.0 s satisfied all the requirements, including the detection of $100\%$ of the reference peaks.

# SNR calculation (T050 usually means peak height / std of baseline in a window around the peak)

# Better: take the noise from a non-peak region, e.g., 200-400 cm-1
noise_region = (x >= 200) & (x <= 400)
sigma_baseline = np.std(y[noise_region])

# Strongest peak intensity relative to baseline
# Use a simple approximation: max(y) - mean(baseline) / sigma_baseline
baseline_mean = np.mean(y[noise_region])
snr = (np.max(y) - baseline_mean) / sigma_baseline
